source.title: Large Language Model Empowered Recommendation Meets All-Domain Continual Pre-Training
source.authors: Haokai Ma; Yun-Shan Ma; Ruo-Bing Xie; Lei Meng; Jia-Lie Shen; Xing-Wu Sun; Zhan-Hui Kang; Tat-seng Chua

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some extracted figures and tables are flattened or garbled; in particular, Figure 5's numerical points cannot be reliably assigned.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies continual-pretraining data volume and measures downstream recommendation performance, bearing on V6, but it does not measure held-out language-model loss or fit the scaling laws in the original sources.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior scaling-law work [1, 47], but reports no results testing those works' loss laws, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocations. Its relevant result is a sweep of continual-pretraining data volume followed by downstream recommendation SFT, with HR@1 plotted in Figure 5.
record.test_reason: This is a recommendation-method paper (CPRec). Its only scale-related result is an internal ablation, Section 5.5.2 and Figure 5. It sweeps the amount of continual-pretraining (CPT) behaviour data (0 to 1M samples, plus the final 'Ours' checkpoint) used to train a LoRA adapter on one fixed LLaMA2-7B. Each checkpoint then gets SFT and is scored by HR@1. The study measures no pretraining loss and fits no curve. It varies no model parameters, tokens or compute in the sense the claim uses. It compares no scaling-law forms. It only says performance 'generally' improves and notes this aligns with recommendation scaling-law papers [1, 47], neither of which is an original source. A five-point ablation of the authors' own method's data volume, with no rate or fit, does not test whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale (V6). The finding is recorded under fits_no_version instead. The reader's T2/tests guess and its V6 limits_scope label are not adopted. That label also rested on parts the study never tested, such as the missing fit and loss link, which belong under untested rather than limits_scope.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say CPRec performance 'would generally improve' with more CPT data, which they say aligns with recommendation scaling-law work [1, 47]. They expect further gains with more data. They also note acceptable results at smaller volumes such as 0.5M, so effectiveness 'is not purely reliant' on data accumulation.
record.recipe_differences: This is a continual-pretraining and recommendation study, not a reproduction of the original language-model loss-scaling or compute-optimal allocation methods.

fits_no_version.finding: For one LLaMA2-7B LoRA setup, adding more continual-pretraining behaviour data (0, 0.1M, 0.2M, 0.5M, 1M, full) before SFT generally raises downstream recommendation HR@1 on five datasets. The authors say 0.5M already gives 'acceptable performance' on some datasets. No fit is reported, and intermediate values can't be read.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream recommendation accuracy of LLM recommenders rises with the volume of continual-pretraining behaviour data (data-scaling of domain CPT).

record.code_released: not stated; the authors say source code will be released upon acceptance.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (provided metadata); the paper body also contains placeholder conference boilerplate.
record.problems: The study measures recommendation HR@1 rather than held-out pretraining loss and uses one LLaMA2-7B backbone. Figure 5's plotted numerical values are not reliably recoverable from the extracted text. The reported four-run averages do not give uncertainty estimates for the Figure 5 sweep.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results left out.

untested.parts: All: no held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no fitted law and no extrapolation.
All: no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
All: no power-law fit in any regime, including continual pretraining.
Predictability of downstream performance from model or pretraining scale or from loss. The only sweep is a non-fitted, five-point ablation of CPT adapter data.
All: no exponents or fitting choices compared.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's main contribution is a CPT framework for LLM recommenders. The originals are only cited, for the cosine schedule (Chinchilla). Figure 5 endpoints coincide with the Table 3 LLaRA and CPRec HR@1 values, but intermediate checkpoints are unreadable in the extracted text. The reported four-seed averages give no uncertainty for the sweep.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run fits or larger-run loss predictions are evaluated.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation sweep is conducted.
No architecture-depth or width comparison at fixed parameter count is reported.
The study uses continual pre-training for recommendation but does not test whether a power-law loss form holds in that regime or another modality.
The study reports downstream HR@1 against continual-pretraining data volume, but does not fit a quantitative predictive relationship or relate performance to pretraining loss.
No comparison of loss-law fitting choices, exponents, curve bending, or compute-optimal allocations is made.
